expectations.text: States the overlap honestly: substantial (~70-80% of controls map) — ISO certification is the best starting point but does NOT substitute for TISAX
expectations.evidence: "About 70 to 80% of the ISA Information Security controls map to ISO 27001:2022"; "an ISO 27001 certificate does not substitute for it"; "best starting point you could have".

expectations.text: Explains the structural differences: fixed maturity targets (0-5, target 3) with cutback rules instead of SoA flexibility; over-performance can't offset weak areas
expectations.evidence: "There is no SoA-style tailoring. Every applicable question must reach target maturity 3... cutback rules mean strong areas cannot offset weak ones."

expectations.text: Identifies the automotive-specific deltas: prototype protection, OEM data-classification expectations, label/exchange mechanics via ENX
expectations.evidence: Table rows: "Prototype Protection module", "Handling of data classified under OEM terms", "Labels and ENX mechanics: Registration, scoping... label sharing, temporary labels and the 9-month corrective window."

expectations.text: Notes ISA2027 refined the ISO 27001:2022 mapping (and removed 2013 references) — map existing evidence first, then close automotive gaps
expectations.evidence: "Both ship with ISO 27001:2022 mappings (ISA2027 also adds NIST CSF 2.0 and drops all 2013 references)"; "Map your ISO evidence to the ISA control areas... Gap-assess what does not map."

expectations.text: Gives a realistic effort estimate for a certified org (evidence re-expression in maturity terms, prototype/physical additions where relevant)
expectations.evidence: "typically months, not a year"; effort tiers Light/Moderate/Heavier — "Re-expressing evidence in maturity terms (0-5)", "Prototype protection (if in scope) and AL3 on-site readiness" heavier.
